## Summary

- Bump the bundled Codex adapter to @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.1.2 and ACPX 0.12.0.
- Change the Codex default to gpt-5.6-sol with max reasoning.
- Adapt model, reasoning, and named-session mode handling to the new adapter contract.
- Keep bundled max coupled to the bundled model, without workflow call-site or explicit-clear changes.

Refs #457.
Supersedes #458.

## Validation

- Node.js 22.13.0: npm run test:ci
  - 754 runtime tests
  - 79 workflow tests
  - 5 docs tests
  - 15 shell tests
- Authenticated one-shot runAcpx smoke returned OK on gpt-5.6-sol[max] without a saved ACPX session.
- Authenticated reconnect smoke retained gpt-5.6-sol[max] and agent-full-access.

| coding_workflow/generic | Prefer Explicit Structured Inputs | pass | 7/7 | The default adds structured `reasoning_effort` instead of encoding all behavior in the model string, and resolver coverage checks model-only overrides do not inherit bundled reasoning in [resolve-agent-provider.test.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/26e0e8d95c6081968f3a15abeb7454f63f042a52/.agent/src/__tests__/resolve-agent-provider.test.ts#L263-L271). |

## Notes

- The implementation matches the linked #457 direction: `gpt-5.6-sol` plus `max`, without treating `ultra` as a plain reasoning-effort value.
- Regression coverage is focused on the resolver and ACPX adapter contracts, including Codex `reasoning_effort`, `agent-full-access`, and `CODEX_CONFIG` behavior.
- The main rubric miss is setup/operator guidance for the new ACPX engine floor. Hosted runners using `node-version: 22` are likely fine, but self-hosted runners pinned to Node 22.0-22.12 can pass Sepo’s current preflight and then fail during runtime install/use.

## Findings

- **WARNING:** The PR upgrades `acpx` to a version requiring Node `>=22.13.0`, but self-hosted docs and setup validation still communicate/accept generic Node 22.x. Update setup guidance and the self-hosted runtime check, or otherwise make the new minimum visible before `npm ci` or ACPX fails.

PARTIAL

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 26e0e8d95c6081968f3a15abeb7454f63f042a52 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #459 implements the linked #457 request by moving Sepo’s bundled Codex default to `gpt-5.6-sol` with `max` reasoning. It also migrates the Codex ACP adapter to `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@1.1.2`, bumps `acpx` to `0.12.0`, and adapts Sepo’s ACPX model/reasoning/session-mode handling to the new adapter contract. The PR supersedes #458 and intentionally avoids the broader explicit-clear workflow changes from that branch. Tests and model/default docs were updated for the new default and adapter behavior.

## Review
The core adapter and resolver direction is sound, and reviewers agreed the default/runtime bump is appropriately bundled. One operational compatibility gap remains: the upgraded ACPX package now requires a stricter Node patch floor than Sepo’s self-hosted setup checks and docs enforce.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Self-hosted Node minimum is not enforced | BLOCKING | `acpx@0.12.0` declares `node >=22.13.0`, but self-hosted setup and local-runner checks still accept generic Node 22.x. Runners on Node 22.0-22.12 can pass Sepo validation and then run an unsupported ACPX runtime. |
| CODEX_CONFIG parse fails opaquely | WARNING | `runAcpx` parses externally settable `CODEX_CONFIG` without a guard. Malformed JSON throws a raw `SyntaxError` before the Codex run starts. |

## Progress
- Current PR checks show `Test Scripts / check` passing on head `26e0e8d95c6081968f3a15abeb7454f63f042a52`.
- The posted rubrics review already acknowledges the Node floor mismatch as a setup/docs gap.
- No existing inline comments or review threads were present before synthesis.
- Posted one inline warning for the `CODEX_CONFIG` parse guard: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/459#discussion_r3557068280.
- No inline replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Self-hosted Node minimum is not enforced</summary>

**Cause:** The PR upgrades `acpx` to `0.12.0`, whose lockfile entry requires Node `>=22.13.0`, but `.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml` still compares only the installed/requested major version. The local runner preflight and README also continue to communicate Node 22.x rather than the patch-level minimum.

**Candidate solutions:** Enforce Node.js `>=22.13.0` in the self-hosted setup action and local-runner requirement check. Update local/self-hosted setup docs that currently say generic Node 22.x.

**Comments:** Codex marked this blocking, rubrics marked it warning/partial, and Claude did not flag it. Current PR head supports the issue: the ACPX engine floor is present in `.agent/package-lock.json`, while the setup action and local runner checks still accept Node 22.0-22.12.

</details>

<details>
<summary>CODEX_CONFIG parse fails opaquely</summary>

**Cause:** `.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts` calls `JSON.parse(env.CODEX_CONFIG?.trim() || "{}")` directly in the Codex run path. If the environment contains malformed `CODEX_CONFIG`, the run fails with a raw parse error before ACPX starts.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a small guarded parser that either falls back to `{}` with a warning or reports a clearer configuration error.

**Comments:** This is a non-blocking robustness issue. I posted it inline because it is tied to a newly changed line and was not already covered in PR discussion.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The Node minimum mismatch requires a concrete branch change and is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Enforce Node.js `>=22.13.0` for self-hosted setup/local-runner checks and update self-hosted/local-runner docs that currently describe generic Node 22.x.
